content:
I have a Lean 4 formalization of Brouwer's fixed-point theorem via Sperner's lemma (Kuhn–Freudenthal grid).
It covers Sperner's lemma in every dimension, Brouwer for the standard simplex, and for any nonempty compact
convex set in finite-dimensional real space. Builds against current mathlib, sorry-free and lint-clean.

To be clear, this isn't the first Lean 4 Brouwer — harfe's fixed-point-theorems-lean4 already has it (general
compact-convex form, via a cubical Sperner). What seems distinct in mine: it routes through the simplicial
Sperner's lemma and exposes "Sperner's lemma in every dimension" as a standalone result, which I don't think
harfe's repo or mathlib has. So the natural mathlib-targeted piece would be simplicial Sperner itself, with
Brouwer derived from it.

It was developed with substantial AI assistance (Claude); I've reviewed it and stand behind it.

Two honest questions:

  1. Would a simplicial Sperner's lemma (as a standalone, library-suitable result) be a welcome contribution to
    mathlib — and is anyone already upstreaming Brouwer (harfe's or otherwise)?

  2. Is there a realistic path for AI-assisted work like this to be merged into mathlib proper, and what's the
    bar?

Code (in my own namespaces):
https://github.com/inventor1975/VRCycle/tree/v1.16-vr-brouwer-v1.0.0/VRCycle/Brouwer

I think there is a realistic path for AI-assisted work to be merged into mathlib (and indeed I'm doing so, and trying to do more), but it is critical to remember that as policy we do not accept AI-assisted PR from "new contributors". So you need to be willing to do the legwork --- and the learning! --- necessary to contribute to mathlib with AI out of the picture, first.

Thanks, Kim — that's genuinely helpful, and the reasoning is fair.

Honestly, you've given me a real decision to weigh rather than a quick yes: the legwork and the learning are substantial, and I'd only want to take that on if I'm sure I'll do it properly rather than half-heartedly.

I'm also mindful that this is all moving fast — you're clearly working to make more AI-assisted contribution possible — so part of what I'm weighing is the right way, and the right moment, to step in. I'll take some time to think it over.

Either way, thank you for the candour, and for actively opening that path.
